previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer, and hypertension was admitted for the third time in a month due to nausea and recurrent bilious vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She presented unable to tolerate oral intake except for ginger ale and had been using compazine at home with partial relief. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics including Reglan and compazine, and insulin adjustment. Her diet was advanced to soft foods by the second hospital day as symptoms improved. Leukocytosis on admission resolved without evidence of infection, attributed to dehydration and stress. Blood pressure was labile; she was restarted on a clonidine patch and continued on lisinopril. She was discharged home in stable condition tolerating oral intake, with instructions to resume all prior medications and follow up with her gastroenterologist and PCP.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
